meta.group: The officers of the first Fort Dearborn on 14 August 1812: Captain Nathan Heald, Lieutenant Linai T. Helm, Ensign George Ronan, surgeon's mate Isaac Van Voorhis; and Captain William Wells, come from Fort Wayne (his Miami escort is T-3467's).
read: AGENTS.md (hard rules, standing constraint), the T-3461 readings (README, garrison.json, native.json, dress.json), the officers' and Wells's household cards, T-3462 place.py (stations, clock) and the 1812 sidecars, doors_1812.json and human-days.js (the span format this file follows: stand/talk/work/walk, knot, spots, to_point).
Quaife 1913 (Gutenberg #69274): ch. VII, ch. X, ch. XI, ch. XIII; App. III (Heald's Journal), IV (Heald's report), V (Darius Heald to Draper, 1868), VI (Helm's narrative and letter).
Wau-Bun (PG 51737, the 1856 text): ch. XVIII and XIX.
Kirkland 1893 (Gutenberg #59624): Part I (Mrs. Heald), Part II ch. III, the Wells scene before p. 94, the plates of Wells (p. 94) and of Darius Heald with the sword (p. 179), App. E.

The 1814 War Department printing of the uniform rules (pp. 262-268) and the 1812 Albany compilation of the Act of 1802 (Sec. 5-6, rations), the local OCR texts T-3461 used.

Looked for a Heald portrait: Wikipedia (none), Wikimedia Commons (rate-limited, not searched), the four books' plate lists (none), a web search (none). Looked for Helm's birth: none found. Hutton 1978 on Wells (Indiana Magazine of History) would not open.
meta.method: Each person carries a presence block (dates in the scene) and `days`: a plain day of 1812 at the post (summer hours, from 1 Jan), for Heald, Helm and Ronan a 13 August evening (Wells comes; the destruction), 14 August, and 15 August until the march at nine. Spans follow renderers/web/js/human-days.js: indoors -> `where` is a structure id (the visitor asks at its door); outdoors -> `at`, `activity` stand|talk|work|walk, with `knot` (talk), `spots` (work) or `to_point` (walk). `with` names other people (other groups' ids: heald_rebekah, helm_margaret, kinzie_john_elder, kinzie_eleanor, black_partridge). `offscene: true` spans are times the person is not in the town at all. Knot ids shared across groups: morning_report, retreat, hired_horses, factory_distribution, second_council_14aug, wagons_14aug, well_destruction, miami_escort; other readers may add their people to them. Every outdoor point was checked to lie outside every 1812 footprint, and away from T-3462's soldier stations.
disagreements_carried: Wells arrived 12 Aug (Helm), 13 Aug (Heald, Quaife, Andreas), 14 Aug (Wau-Bun, Currey). Heald followed, as the cards do. The battle jaunt's stop "the-gate" has Wells ride in at sunset on the 14th (Wau-Bun's date); the 14 August scene here has him in the fort since the 13th.
Factory goods given out on the 14th (Heald, Quaife) or the 13th (Wau-Bun, the battle jaunt). Heald followed.
Arms, powder and liquor destroyed the night of the 13th (Helm, Wau-Bun, Andreas); Heald's report does not date it. The tail of the work is put past midnight into the 14th.
First council 12th (Wau-Bun) or probably 13th (Quaife); a second on the afternoon of the 14th (Wau-Bun, Currey). Helm makes Wells the leader of a council; Quaife thinks Heald.

Black Partridge: 'evening' (Wau-Bun, Andreas) or 'night' (Helm) of the 14th; to the commander's quarters (Wau-Bun, Andreas) or 'the officers' quarters' (Currey); the interpreter unnamed (Helm) or Kinzie (Currey).
Van Voorhis born 22 Feb 1790 (genealogy, 1881) vs 'born 1789' on his card (from Quaife's 'twenty-two' in Oct 1811). The genealogy is taken.

Wau-Bun's officers' 'unanimous advice' against leaving and its feud between Heald and Ronan; Mrs. Heald (via Darius, Kirkland) denied both. Neither acted out; the officers are given their work, not a quarrel.
Provisions: Wau-Bun's Heald says he has 'no salt' to keep the beef; Helm counts '27 barrels of Salt' and 200 head of cattle. Not needed for the day; noted.
meta.liberty: Proposed liberty L-1812-officers-day-3463: every hour, place and companion in the officers' days is reconstructed unless a span is graded otherwise; the second council's blockhouse arrangement repeats Wau-Bun's 12th; Wells's escort point is a fallback; the ensign's epaulette and the Wells dress are ours. Nothing of the day is acted out beyond where people stand and what they are at (L1).

people.name: Nathan Heald
people.role: Captain, First Infantry, commanding the post

present.basis: His own report of 23 Oct 1812 tells what he did on the 14th.

presence.basis: Journal: to Chicago 'In June 1810'; on furlough from the fall of 1810, back 'in June' 1811 with his wife; marched out on 15 August 1812. Day of the month ours.

gaps.basis: Furlough 'in the fall' of 1810 to June 1811 (Journal); the days are ours.

age_1812.basis: Born 24 September 1775 (his Journal); 36 on 14 August 1812. Currey says 37.

home.basis: The commanding officer's quarters on the east side (Whistler's index; Quaife); Wau-Bun, Helm, Andreas and Currey all put Black Partridge's visit there.

looks.basis: No likeness of him exists: his son told Draper in 1868 'There is no likeness extant of Maj. Heald.' None is in Kirkland (1893), Currey (1912), Quaife (1913) or Andreas (1884), and none was found on Wikipedia or Commons (2026-11-08). So his colouring is from his New Hampshire family of English descent and his height near the period's mean (68.1 in, T-3491). The 1893 photograph of his son Darius with the relics shows the son, not him.
looks.portrait_note: The brief expected a Heald portrait; none exists that the sources know of. Rebekah Heald's daguerreotype (Quaife plate; Currey plate) is hers, in later life.

officer_first_infantry_1812.pieces: Coat of dark blue superfine cloth, single-breasted, skirts to the bend of the knee, white turnbacks; standing collar to the ear and cuffs of scarlet, with silver lace loops on the collar; white-metal (silver) buttons. One silver bullion epaulette: Heald (captain) on the RIGHT shoulder; Helm (second lieutenant) on the LEFT; Ronan (ensign) on the LEFT as a lieutenant (no source for an ensign's; ours). White waistcoat; white linen pantaloons or breeches (summer); black stock; boots to the knee. Black felt chapeau bras worn fore and aft, black cockade with an eagle, white feather. Sword on a white leather waist belt: Heald's is the curved, stirrup-hilted sword with a knot that Darius Heald holds in Kirkland's 1893 photograph (the 'Heald's sword' Quaife says the family kept); Helm's and Ronan's straight, brass-mounted (by analogy). Crimson silk sash round the waist ONLY on a tour of duty (officer of the day, a council, the march).

states.duty: Coat buttoned, chapeau, sword, sash. Heald at the factory, the council and in the evening when Black Partridge comes; Ronan all day on 14 August (officer of the day); everyone at the morning report, retreat and on the 15th.
states.undress: Coat worn open over the waistcoat, no sash; chapeau or a round hat; sword left in quarters. Helm and Van Voorhis at work about the post, and everyone on the plain day off duty.
states.march_15: Heald wears the 'regular military suit' with a wamus (a short jacket) under it, holding money Rebekah sewed into it (Darius Heald). Helm carries a gun ('the barrel of my gun') and wears a lined coat with pockets (his 1814 narrative).

wells_frontier_agent_1812.builds_on: nothing in dress.json (it leaves Native dress to native.json and has no frontier agent). New role.
wells_frontier_agent_1812.pieces: A man of the frontier who had lived among the Miami from boyhood. Hair long, in a queue tied with black ribbon (Wau-Bun, of his scalp on the 15th). A round felt hat (he waved his hat, Darius Heald). Linen or calico shirt; a hunting frock or a short blue cloth coat; breechcloth, cloth leggings and moccasins (he was 'dressed like an Indian' on the 15th, Darius Heald; on the 14th the same dress is ours, as the man who rode with the Miami across the country). Belt with a dirk; a pistol; a rifle (all three in the accounts of the 15th). Rides a pony. On the 15th only: face blackened (Wau-Bun, Darius Heald, Currey).
wells_frontier_agent_1812.alternative: The plates captioned 'William Wells' in Kirkland (1893) and Currey (1912) show a man in an officer's coat with a high laced collar, one epaulette, a ruffled shirt and black stock, which would be his dress as a captain of scouts under Wayne in the 1790s if the picture is his. Its origin is not given. Owner to choose (see summary); we recommend the frontier dress for August 1812.
wells_frontier_agent_1812.colours: hat black or brown felt; shirt white or printed calico; frock or coat blue; leggings blue or red stroud; moccasins smoked brown; queue ribbon black.
wells_frontier_agent_1812.grade_note: The queue, the hat, the weapons and the blackened face of the 15th are attested; the cut and colours of the clothes are ours.
